meta.desc: P2-H: authoritative open sources for the domains whose lessons are mostly tutor-written (docs/NIGHT_PLAN.md P2-H). Merged into each module's reading list (curriculum.json) and sent to the tutor with the module. Each item names its module and topic.
meta.link_check: curl -sSIL through the session proxy on 2026-10-30 (GET fallback). status: ok = HTTP 200/206; doi = DOI registered and title/author matched in Crossref (publisher site may refuse scripts); blocked = the site returns 403/202 to scripts, title and URL confirmed by web search; it opens in a browser.
meta.early_review: These domains get the first external review in the first weekly review that reaches them (P2-E).

items.topic: JADC2/CJADC2 claims vs measurable latency
items.title: Battle Management: DOD and Air Force Continue to Define Joint Command and Control Efforts (GAO-23-105495)
items.why: The official evidence base on what multi-domain C2 programs have actually delivered versus what is claimed; the reference point for any latency or capability claim about networked C2.
items.focus: Highlights and the sections on ABMS requirements, cost and schedule; note which capabilities still have no defined delivery date.

items.topic: C2 data sharing and network architecture
items.title: Defense Command and Control: Further Progress Hinges on Establishing a Comprehensive Framework (GAO-25-106454)
items.why: Follow-up on CJADC2: data-sharing between existing systems, classification as an engineering constraint on information flow.
items.focus: What GAO found on data standards and classification barriers; compare with the 2023 report.

items.topic: Kill webs and distributed sensor-to-effector architectures (NIFC-CA case)
items.title: Distributed Kill Chains: Drawing Insights for Mosaic Warfare from the Immune System and from the Navy (RR-A573-1)
items.authors: N. A. O'Donoughue, S. McBirney, B. Persons
items.why: A documented engineering case (NIFC-CA engage-on-remote) of a distributed sensor-to-effector chain: what made it work, measured against the mosaic concept.
items.focus: The NIFC-CA case study chapter and the recommendations; read for timing, track quality and test infrastructure.

items.topic: Decision cycles (OODA) and tempo
items.title: Patterns of Conflict (briefing)
items.why: The primary source of the OODA loop; needed to separate what Boyd argued from how 'decision cycle' is used loosely in C2 program claims.
items.focus: The slides on the observe-orient-decide-act loop and on tempo; skip the historical survey.

items.topic: JDL data-fusion levels
items.title: An Introduction to Multisensor Data Fusion
items.why: The standard reference for the JDL fusion model (levels 0-4) that every C4ISR architecture description uses.
items.focus: The JDL model section and the table of fusion algorithms by level.

items.topic: Joint targeting cycle, target development and collateral damage estimation methodology
items.title: JP 3-60 Joint Targeting (31 January 2013)
items.why: The doctrinal description of the six-phase targeting cycle, combat assessment and the CDE methodology, as a process model with inputs, outputs and decision points.
items.focus: Ch. II (the joint targeting cycle) and the appendix on collateral damage estimation as a method; read as a process-engineering description.

items.topic: Battle damage assessment and its biases; claims vs evidence
items.title: Operation Desert Storm: Evaluation of the Air Campaign (GAO/NSIAD-97-134)
items.why: The classic audit of effectiveness claims against post-war data: how BDA overstated results and why sparse effectiveness data limits the lessons.
items.focus: The results-in-brief and the chapters comparing claimed with verified effects and on the reliability of damage assessment.

items.topic: Consumption, LOC capacity and logistics models
items.title: Operational Logistics: The Art and Science of Sustaining Military Operations, 2nd ed.
items.why: The NPS operations-research textbook on logistics: quantitative models of consumption, distribution networks and sustainment capacity, the tool missing from van Creveld's history.
items.focus: The chapters on logistics capability measures and on the quantitative models (consumption rates, transport capacity, network flow).

items.topic: Sustainment functions, distribution and readiness (doctrinal process model)
items.title: JP 4-0 Joint Logistics (4 February 2019, incorporating Change 1)
items.why: The official taxonomy of logistics functions and the logistics estimate; the vocabulary used by GAO, CBO and RAND sustainment studies.
items.focus: Ch. I-II (core logistic functions, the joint logistics environment) and the logistics estimate appendix.

items.topic: Munitions consumption vs stockpiles in a high-intensity war
items.title: Preliminary Lessons in Conventional Warfighting from Russia's Invasion of Ukraine: February-July 2022
items.authors: M. Zabrodskyi, J. Watling, O. V. Danylyuk, N. Reynolds
items.why: Measured artillery and munitions consumption rates from a current high-intensity war: the input numbers for any stockpile or production-rate calculation.
items.focus: The sections on fires and on logistics and sustainment; extract the consumption figures and their sources.

items.topic: Russian ground-force structure and how it fights (as a system)
items.title: The Russian Way of War: Force Structure, Tactics, and Modernization of the Russian Ground Forces
items.authors: L. W. Grau, C. K. Bartles
items.why: The most detailed open description of Russian ground-force organization, equipment and doctrine by the Army's foreign-military analysts; the reference for M12.2 beyond the ATP.
items.focus: The chapters on force structure, fires and air defense; read for the system parameters (organization, ranges, sensor-to-shooter links). Official copy on the FMSO bookshelf (APAN); the archive.org copy is v1.2 (2017).

items.topic: Russian military strategy and operational concepts
items.title: Russian Military Strategy: Core Tenets and Operational Concepts
items.authors: M. Kofman, A. Fink, D. Gorenburg, M. Chesnut, J. Edmonds, J. Waller
items.why: The standard open synthesis of Russian military thought from Russian-language sources; frames the air-defense and EW systems of M12.1 inside the concept they serve.
items.focus: The chapters on the strategic operation for destruction of critically important targets and on aerospace defense.

items.topic: PLA modernization and organization (capability assessment)
items.title: China Military Power: Modernizing a Force to Fight and Win
items.why: An official, illustrated capability baseline of PLA forces and organization after the 2015-16 reforms; complements the annual DoD report already in the list (M12.3).
items.focus: The chapters on PLA organization, the ground force and the rocket force; compare parameters with D6.

items.topic: Blast loads, fragment velocity and penetration (engineering design data)
items.title: UFC 3-340-02 Structures to Resist the Effects of Accidental Explosions
items.why: The open engineering standard for blast pressure-impulse loads, scaled distance, primary fragment velocity (Gurney form) and fragment penetration; the quantitative source this domain lacked.
items.focus: Ch. 2 (blast, fragment and shock loads: scaled distance, pressure and impulse charts, fragment velocity and mass distribution); read as protective-design data.

items.topic: Effectiveness methods: Pk from CEP, lethal area, expected damage
items.title: Weaponeering: An Introduction to Weapon System Effectiveness, 3rd ed.
items.why: The NPS textbook of the effectiveness methodology (delivery accuracy, CEP, lethal area, damage functions) behind M11.4, at a quantitative level the library's sources do not reach.
items.focus: The chapters on delivery accuracy and CEP, target vulnerability and lethal area, and the single-weapon and multiple-weapon effectiveness calculations.

items.topic: Interior, exterior and terminal ballistics
items.title: Ballistics: Theory and Design of Guns and Ammunition, 3rd ed.
items.authors: D. E. Carlucci, S. S. Jacobson
items.why: The standard engineering textbook of gun and projectile ballistics, from interior ballistics through flight dynamics to terminal ballistics.
items.focus: Exterior ballistics (drag, stability) and the terminal-ballistics chapters; use the worked examples to check the module's calculations.

items.topic: Armour materials and penetration mechanics
items.title: Armour: Materials, Theory, and Design, 2nd ed.
items.why: The materials-science view of protection: penetration mechanics, ceramics and composites, shaped-charge jet interaction; the depth behind the protection onion of M11.6.
items.focus: The chapters on penetration mechanics and on ceramic and composite armour.

items.topic: Per-unit, three-phase, power flow and faults (course)
items.title: 6.061 Introduction to Electric Power Systems (lecture notes)
items.why: No book in the library teaches grids; these free MIT notes give the BSc-level core (phasors, three-phase, per-unit, transmission lines, power flow) the tutor builds the module on.
items.focus: Lecture notes on three-phase systems, per-unit, transmission lines and power flow; the problem sets for checking numbers.

items.topic: Power-flow and contingency studies in code
items.title: pandapower: An Open Source Python Tool for Convenient Modeling, Analysis and Optimization of Electric Power Systems
items.why: The open tool the benchmark names for the module's next-level project (a load-flow and contingency study); the paper explains its element models and solvers.
items.focus: Sections on the element models and the power-flow solver; then run one of the example networks.

items.topic: Finite element method: formulation and practice
items.title: 2.092 Finite Element Analysis of Solids and Fluids I (video lectures and notes)
items.why: FEM taught by the author of the standard text: the principle of virtual work, element matrices, convergence, and how to judge an FEM result.
items.focus: Lectures 1-6 (formulation, element matrices, convergence) and the lecture on modeling errors.

items.topic: Weak forms and Galerkin FEM in code
items.title: Solving PDEs in Python: The FEniCS Tutorial I
items.why: Open-access, written by the author of the library's finite-difference book (E08): weak form, Galerkin discretization and verification in a few lines of code.
items.focus: Ch. 2-3 (Poisson problem, weak form, verification) and the elasticity example.

items.topic: Ritz-Galerkin and finite elements from linear algebra
items.title: 18.085 Computational Science and Engineering I
items.why: Strang's route to finite elements through stiffness matrices and K = A^T C A; links M10.10 to the linear algebra of P8.
items.focus: The lectures on finite elements in 1D and 2D and on the stiffness matrix.
